//: The bot's settings: the only place any loop value is set. Copy to the repo root as opsbot.json, fill in, commit, then run `scripts/opsbot-core settings validate`. A "//" key is a comment and is allowed at any level. Values below are examples.
name: examplebot

loop.//: prompt is sent verbatim by the nudge; include any cold-cache suffix your setup uses. mode (strategist or dispatcher) picks the model and the compaction window; set loop.model or loop.autocompact only to override it. schedule is self (the default: the session schedules its own wakeup with this prompt) or monitor (one bounded Monitor armed at the end of every cycle wakes it when a wake file grows or the next cycle is due; the prompt must then be a plain message, not a slash command, and the nudge defaults tighten to 35 minutes).
loop.prompt: /loop examplebot cycle. Follow the opsbot-core skill: start with `cycle begin`.

cadence.//: Seconds. None may exceed cap; cap stays under the one-hour cache. Hours are in timezone; days are ISO weekdays (1 = Monday). A dispatcher with wake.files can drop quiet_working and quiet: they then default to the cap, since its streams wake it.

liveness.//: watchdog_minutes: no cycle for this long is an outage. nudge_minutes: quiet this long earns a nudge. interval_minutes: how often both timers fire.

streams.//: Per-stream values the heartbeat scripts in opsbot.d/heartbeat.d/ read through $OPSBOT_CONFIG. The core does not look inside.

memory.//: Claude Code's auto memory, kept in this repo: start points the session at dir (repo-relative) and every cycle commits it. review_days: how long after the last review the next one is due. Both optional, defaults shown. Set "memory": false to turn auto memory off; nothing leaves it at Claude Code's default location outside the repo.
